body:
Follow-up to #1957. Two things, both consequences of that PR rather than new work.

## 1. The carve-out the #1957 review raised

The G8 gate shipped matching fork citations with `/#(\d{3,4})\b/g` — a bound fitted to the id shape of every open decision at the time. `norm` strips leading zeros, so `we:backlog/039-*.md` has id `39`, and **98 items** carry a 1–2 digit normalized id the bound could never see. A fork leaning on one of them read as clear.

Widened to `/#(\d+)\b/g`.

**Measured, not assumed:** the live G8 count is **9 before, 9 after** across 3,496 items — no currently-open decision has a short id, so this is inert on today's corpus and correct going forward. No false positives appeared either.

Two tests pin **both** ends of the range, because the defect was a bound nobody was watching:

- a 1–2 digit id (`#39`) — the case that was blind;
- a 4-digit id (`#3512`) — so widening the low end can't silently drop the high end.

**Mutation-verified, both directions:** restoring `\d{3,4}` reddens the 1–2 digit test; `\d{1,3}` reddens the 4-digit test. Neither assertion is decorative.

The juror's disposition on this finding was `carve-out` (`introduced: true`, `worseThanBase: false`, `parallelizable: true`), which is why it lands here as its own diff rather than as a late push onto the reviewed head of #1957.

## 2. Nine stranded hashes, numbered

#1957 was opened through the credential-less fallback rather than `pr-land`, so the drain's JIT numbering (#2288) never ran and nine cards landed on `main` still carrying their hash ids. `npm run check:standards` was **red on `main`** as a result — nine `#2319` stranded-hash errors.

`node we:scripts/backlog.mjs number-stranded` healed it:

| was | now |
| --- | --- |
| `x2xrboe` | **#3513** |
| `x5c8zep` | **#3514** |
| `x6z6z2j` | **#3515** |
| `xarvjgf` | **#3516** |
| `xayr3dc` | **#3517** |
| `xblcmkc` | **#3518** |
| `xbwup67` | **#3519** |
| `xjktyol` | **#3520** |
| `xzdzg3j` | **#3521** |

Each keeps a `bornAs:` lineage stamp, and the cross-references were rewritten with the rename (`#3519`'s `crossRef` now points at `/backlog/3513-…/`, not the dead hash path). Verified by grep: the only surviving hash mentions are the `bornAs:` stamps themselves.

## 3. Filed, not fixed: `xs10j09`

`G1` and `D2` carry the **same defect class, worse**. Both walk citations with `\d{1,3}\b`:

```js
// we:scripts/audit-backlog-health.mjs lines 129–130
const PROSE_PREREQ = /\b(gated on|blocked on|…)\s+#?(\d{1,3})\b/gi;   // G1
const ANY_REF      = /(?:#|\/backlog\/)(\d{1,3})\b/g;                 // D2, and two other walks
```

`\d{1,3}\b` cannot match `#2209` **at all** — the engine takes `220`, finds no word boundary before `9`, backtracks to `22` and `2`, fails each time, and reports no match. It misses; it does not truncate. The board runs to **#3521**, so the bound is blind to the majority of the corpus. Consistent with what the counts show: **D2 = 1** across 3,496 items reads as a clean board and is instead a gate that stopped seeing.

Confirmed by running both literals against a case table, not by reading the patterns:

| citation | `ANY_REF` (G1/D2) | G8 after this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `#39` | `39` | `39` |
| `#607` | `607` | `607` |
| `#2209` | *(nothing)* | `2209` |
| `#3512` | *(nothing)* | `3512` |

Both regexes are live — `ANY_REF` at lines 336, 365, 522; `PROSE_PREREQ` at line 425 — so this is not a dead definition. **Filed rather than fixed here** because it is pre-existing, sits in gates this diff does not touch, and widening it changes what G1 and D2 report board-wide. That is a measurement change owed its own before/after count, not a rider on this one. `xs10j09` carries the evidence and the trap: unlike G8, these will **not** be inert when widened.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run` — **409 files, 10,766 passed / 7 skipped, 0 failed** (the two new G8 cases are the delta).
- `we:scripts/__tests__/audit-backlog-health.test.mjs` — 12/12.
- `npm run check:standards` with `WE_SKIP_HAND_NUMBERED_GATE=1` (the sanctioned renumbering path the gate's own message names, #2548) — the 9 hand-numbered errors clear. The 9 remaining *"is on main with a NON-NUMERIC leading id"* errors are the transitional state by construction: those files are still on `origin/main` until this PR lands, which is what clears them.
- `node we:scripts/check-backlog-item.mjs xs10j09` — clean.

## Known limit

Same as #1957: no `gh` credential on this host, so the PR was opened through the API rather than `pr-land`. The **decision** still came from the operation — `scoreEscalation` returns `escalate: true`, `humanRequired: false` (blast-radius on the two `scripts/` files) → `producerReviewLabel` = **`review:pending`**, applied by hand at open. The `authored-by-actor` stamp is absent and no independence guard runs at open (#3267). This PR is the second instance of that cost; the first one's is what section 2 cleans up.
